clue.text: Bad-tempered driver clipping rear of another

indicators.note: to clip something is to fasten round it, so the driver holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, so only the end of another is kept

parts.note: last letter of another

explanation.surface: A grumpy motorist cuts in and clips the back of somebody else's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal synonym for irritable, like a crab snapping its claws.

clue.text: Maybe saw scanner checking ambassador's head

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so the scanner restrains what follows within itself

parts.note: a CT scanner takes computed tomography images
HE, His Excellency, is an ambassador's title; with the 's
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A security scanner checks an ambassador's head at the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador. A saw is an old saying, and a stale, overused saying is one kind of the answer, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale story or proverb repeated too often, and an old saw is one example of it.

clue.text: Draws return game 50-50, inspired by host

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so everything after it is read from the end
something inspired is breathed in, so these letters go inside the host word

parts.note: a sea of people is a host, a great multitude
RU is Rugby Union
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, twice

explanation.surface: A sports report: a drawn return match, the points split evenly, with the home side as inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like the result of the return game, but it is a verb meaning attracts. 'Return' applies to everything after it, so the whole assembly is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to tempt or entice, so allures and draws both mean attracts in the third person.

clue.text: Trains essentially went all over the place under British Rail

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means following it on the way down

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: scattered all over the place means in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central part, so only the middle of went is kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of went

explanation.surface: Trains ran haywire under the old nationalised British Rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Rail' reads as the old train operator, but it splits: British gives B and Rail is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bannister is the handrail running up the side of a staircase.

clue.text: Knocking back the booze? Order Carol's round

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the song word encloses the command word

parts.note: to carol is to sing; the 's is 'is'
a will is a command or decree

explanation.surface: A drinker ordering: it is Carol's turn to buy the round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' and 'round' look like a trip to the bar, but round is the enclosing signal and Carol is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Swilling means gulping drink greedily, which is knocking back alcohol.

clue.text: Secure title with scores engineered in period of low light?

indicators.note: something engineered has been rebuilt to a new design, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to win something is to secure it
the letters of title and scores, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sportsperson secures a title and runs up big scores during a bad patch of form.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'low light' is a fanciful description: the shortest day has the least daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter solstice in December is the day with the fewest hours of daylight in the year.

clue.text: Insect repellent's core requirement on river

indicators.note: what is required is the core, the very centre letter of the word before

parts.note: the central letter of the nine-letter word repellent
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Insect repellent is just what you need by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect repellent' reads as one phrase, but it splits: Insect is the definition and repellent supplies its central letter, which sits on top of the river in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless parasitic insect living on mammals and birds.

clue.text: Number one governor from the south promoting north

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means going upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a regent governs on behalf of a monarch

explanation.surface: A political report: the number one governor comes from the south and promotes a northerner.
explanation.walkthrough: After the word for governor is read upwards, 'promoting north' moves its N (north) up one place, to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: Organs of state entering case for governments

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so the first word sits within the second
a case is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of governments
a land is a country or state

explanation.surface: Organs of the state making a case to governments sounds like civil-service lobbying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organs of state' reads as government bodies; here Organs alone is the definition, in its anatomical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Glands are bodily organs that secrete hormones or other substances.

clue.text: Material's clean and appropriate for the audience

parts.note: something clean is free of marks

indicators.note: what is meant for an audience is heard rather than read, so the second word goes by its sound

parts.note: to appropriate is to take without permission

explanation.surface: A costume designer insists the fabric be clean and suitable for the people watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but works as a verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel is a rust-resistant alloy, a material used for cutlery and sinks.

clue.text: Bandleader John possibly admitting uninitiated affair

indicators.note: without its initial, so the word loses its first letter
admitting someone lets them in, so the singer's name surrounds what follows

parts.note: Elton John, the singer; 'possibly' says John is one example
a fling is a brief affair; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A gossip item: a famous bandleader called John admits to an affair with an inexperienced partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John possibly' points to a surname, not a first name: Elton is one John.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was a celebrated American jazz bandleader and composer.

clue.text: Uber taxi's beginning to cut university student price (50 per cent off)

indicators.note: removing half means dropping the second half of the word
to cut into something is to break into it, so the single letter goes inside

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
L is a learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so just that is kept

parts.note: first letter of taxi
rate is a price; half of it stays

explanation.surface: Uber cuts student taxi fares in half for the university crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uber' reads as the ride-hailing firm, but it is the definition: German über, meaning super or extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Uber as a prefix means super or extreme, just as ultra does.

clue.text: Stops car after stint sharing miles

indicators.note: if two words share a letter it appears only once where they meet, so one copy goes
one thing coming after another puts the vehicle second, behind the period of work

parts.note: a term is a fixed period, a stint
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A car journey after a long stint behind the wheel, sharing the mileage.
explanation.walkthrough: The words end and start with M (miles), and that M is shared, so it appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of lines, plural of terminus, so stops at the end.

clue.text: Turned up hem in the middle and knitted

indicators.note: only the central letter of the short word is wanted

parts.note: the middle letter of hem
things knitted together are joined, merged

explanation.surface: A sewing scene: a hem was turned up in the middle and knitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up hem' reads as a sewing job, but Turned up is the definition, meaning appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to appear or arrive, and to emerge is to come into view.

clue.text: Trouble from appendix during puberty occasionally

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the first item goes inside the second
something done occasionally happens every so often, so only alternate letters are kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of puberty
a PS, postscript, is an appendix to a letter

explanation.surface: A doctor's note: appendix trouble that flares up now and then during adolescence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appendix' suggests the organ; here it is the postscript at the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as a noun means a disturbance or trouble, as in a stomach upset.

clue.text: Culmination of quarrel over daughter started by Oxford model?

indicators.note: something started by another has that other placed at its front

parts.note: an Oxford is a shoe, and a last is the foot-shaped model a shoe is made on

indicators.note: a thing turned over is upside down, so the quarrel word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family row about a daughter, sparked by an Oxford-educated model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Culmination of quarrel' looks like a description of having the final say, but only Culmination is the definition; 'Oxford model' is a shoe last, not a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: The last word in something is its most advanced or ultimate form, its peak.

clue.text: Total of all he owes written off

indicators.note: a written-off car is wrecked, so these letters are smashed up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, ready to rearrange

explanation.surface: A debtor has every penny of his debt written off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total' looks like the sum owed, but it is an adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale used as an adjective means extensive and indiscriminate, as in wholesale slaughter, so complete.

clue.text: Perhaps Cuban heels finally breaking near Lidl, virtually ruined

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the store name is not quite complete
to break into something is to get inside it, so the single letter goes within
something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
the supermarket name minus its last letter

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

parts.note: last letter of heels

explanation.surface: A Cuban breaks a heel near a Lidl store and is nearly ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Lidl is a discount supermarket chain. 'Perhaps' says Cuban is one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island nation, so a Cuban is an example of someone who lives on an island.

clue.text: Legitimate to claim jail not working as act of retribution

indicators.note: working can be expressed as on, and 'not' that means those letters are removed
to claim something is to take hold of it, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: something legitimate is genuine, real
prison, with ON (working) dropped

explanation.surface: Someone lawfully claims a jail is failing, as an act of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: On means working, as a machine that is on; taking it from the jail word leaves PRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is retaliation, an act of revenge in return for an injury.

clue.text: Cheer enthralling start to Manchester United match

indicators.note: something enthralling holds you captive, so the cheer word holds the initials inside

parts.note: to elate is to cheer, make happy

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter, so only the initials of the club name are kept

parts.note: the initials of the football club

explanation.surface: Supporters cheer an exciting opening to a Manchester United match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like the football game, but it is a verb meaning to equal.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or rival them, which is matching them.

clue.text: Unseats first character from contests with aim to unseat the other?

indicators.note: taking the first character from a word means dropping its opening letter

parts.words: contests with aim to unseat the other
parts.note: jousts, mounted contests aiming to knock the rival off his horse, without the J

explanation.surface: Riders in a tournament each try to knock the other off his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The long cryptic description is of jousts; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to remove someone from a position, which is to unseat them.

clue.text: Spirited horse pounding 1,000 metres should be checked

indicators.note: a horse pounding a stretch of track covers it entirely, so it goes round the units

parts.note: Chambers defines a steed as a spirited horse
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
m is the abbreviation for metres

explanation.surface: A lively racehorse galloping a kilometre ought to be reined in.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or stop it, so stemmed means checked.

clue.text: Facing workers' organisation, company boss ultimately superior

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means higher, so this letter is placed on top
ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of boss is kept

parts.note: last letter of boss
the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A union faces off with the company, whose boss believes they are superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' sounds like confronting; it is the definition, a noun for a wall covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a plaster coating applied to the outside walls of a building as a facing.

clue.text: Disturbs pets

definitions.meaning: second meaning: strokes or handles gently

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like a noun for animals, but it is a verb, to stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean affects someone emotionally and also lays a hand on, as with stroking.

clue.text: One putting up prices steeply in March meeting resistance

indicators.note: two things meeting come together side by side, so one piece joins the end of the other

parts.note: to hike is to march a long way
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Steep price rises in March meet resistance from consumers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' with its capital looks like the month; it is the verb. The definition is a fanciful one, someone who hikes prices; the walker climbing hills lurks behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike prices is to raise them sharply, so a hiker would be one who does that.

clue.text: Attracted to that place, like to go back in May?

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the short word is read from its end

parts.note: as means like

explanation.surface: Someone drawn to a place wants to return there in the spring month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: May is not the month but the surname of Theresa May, the former UK Prime Minister; her first name is what you find in May's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is the first name of the politician May, so it is part of her name.

clue.text: Create division with skilful or witty remark

definitions.meaning: first meaning: split, open a fissure
second meaning: expert, first-rate, as of a marksman
third meaning: a wisecrack or quip

explanation.walkthrough: This has three separate meanings, joined by with and or.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for splitting, an adjective for expert, and a noun for a joke.

clue.text: Came out with or without medical supply?

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb of supple, so the word bends flexibly into a new form

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
its letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether to leave with or without their medical supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun for stock, but it is an adverb, in a supple way.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so came out with in speech means said aloud forcefully.

clue.text: What VAR could do with public order, taking time out

indicators.note: taking something out removes it, and time is the letter T

parts.note: overt means public; T, time, is removed
a rule is an order or regulation

explanation.surface: Football's video referee could impose public order by stopping the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is the Video Assistant Referee in football, who reviews and can reverse on-field decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule is to reverse a decision by superior authority, which the video referee may cause.

clue.text: One holding Kindle say, changing hands to find article

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so the right is swapped for the left

parts.note: a Kindle is an e-reader, and its user is a reader; R becomes L

explanation.surface: A Kindle owner switches it between hands to locate an article.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle is Amazon's e-book device. The R (right) of the word is replaced with L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper's main editorial article.
